definitions.explanation: Having mental or spiritual strength; being able to overcome difficulties.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はたくましい{体|からだ}をしている。
{息子|むすこ}がたくましく{成長|せいちょう}した。
examples.english: My son has grown up strong.

examples.japanese: たくましい{精神|せいしん}で{困難|こんなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: With a resilient spirit, I overcame the difficulties.

notes:
FORMS:
・Adverbial: たくましく (sturdily, strongly)
・Noun form: たくましさ (sturdiness, robustness)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・たくましい{体|からだ}/{腕|うで} (sturdy body/arms)
・たくましく{育|そだ}つ/{成長|せいちょう}する (to grow up strong)
・たくましい{精神力|せいしんりょく} (strong willpower)

KANJI FORM:
{逞|たくま}しい exists but hiragana is standard.

NUANCE:
Positive connotation. For physical strength, implies healthy, muscular build rather than just size. For mental strength, implies resilience and the ability to thrive despite challenges.

CONTRAST:
・たくましい: emphasizes robust strength and vitality
・{強|つよ}い: general strength
・{頑丈|がんじょう}: durability, solidness
